findings.label: r/g2074788f713e-2-1
findings.reason: The change removes the line that defines the reading as the maximum of the wall clock and the anchor plus monotonic elapsed time, which contradicts the rejected alternative of freezing the clock until the wall clock catches up after a backward step.
findings.text:
Rejected: Freeze the clock until the wall clock catches up after a backward step.
The monotonic branch keeps advancing at the oscillator's rate instead.

findings.label: r/g2074788f713e-2-2
findings.reason: The change removes the line that defines the reading as the maximum of the wall clock and the anchor plus monotonic elapsed time, which contradicts the rejected alternative of refusing a forward jump because it disagrees with the monotonic projection.
findings.text:
Rejected: Refuse a forward jump because it disagrees with the monotonic projection.
A forward jump is a correction arriving; refusing would prefer this process's opinion to the system's.

findings.label: d/g2074788f713e-1
findings.reason: The change removes the line that defines the reading as the maximum of the wall clock and the anchor plus monotonic elapsed time, which contradicts the decision to route all time readings through a process-wide session clock.
findings.text:
Route all time readings through a process-wide session clock.
The system clock can step backwards due to NTP, VM resume, or operator; a continuously running wallclock would show time going backward. The session clock ensures one monotonic reading order.
